question.value: What are the H2CO emission morphologies, excitation temperatures and column densities across 15 protoplanetary disks, and what do they imply about H2CO formation (gas-phase vs CO-ice hydrogenation)?

evidence.quote: We characterize the H$_2$CO morphologies, excitation temperatures, and column densities, evaluate their dependence on stellar and disk characteristics, and assess the chemical origins of H$_2$CO.

pipeline_or_manual.value: Initial calibration by ALMA/NAASC staff; then self-calibration in CASA

evidence.quote: The ALMA/NAASC staff performed the initial calibration (including bandpass, flux, and phase calibration) for each observation.
we used the COMMON ASTRONOMY SOFTWARE APPLICATIONS package (CASA) version 4.7.2 to self-calibrate and image each targeted line.

flux_scale_uncertainty.value: 10% absolute flux uncertainty added in quadrature in rotational diagram fits

evidence.quote: Errors and fits include 10% absolute flux uncertainties, added in quadrature to the velocity-integrated flux uncertainties.

self_calibration.value: Continuum from all spectral windows after removing strong lines; solint 10-100 s; 2 phase + 1 amplitude iterations; robust 0.5; exceptions for some lines

evidence.quote: We carried out 2 iterations of phase calibration and 1 iteration of amplitude calibration for each line, and we used a Briggs weighting scheme and a robust value of 0.5 during the self-calibration process for all disks.
imaged each targeted line using CASA’s `clean` algorithm

weighting_robust.value: Briggs robust 0.5; weaker tentative/non-detected lines reimaged with robust=2

evidence.quote: The weaker H$_2$CO lines that were tentatively-detected or non-detected with robust=0.5 were reimaged with robust=2 to maximize sensitivity.

uv_taper.value: 0.25-0.60 arcsec tapers for some lines (IM Lup, V4046 Sgr, MWC 480, HD 163296, DM Tau)

evidence.quote: 0.25" for the H$_2$CO 4$_{04}$-3$_{03}$ line towards IM Lup and V4046 Sgr, 0.40" for the 5$_{15}$-4$_{14}$ line towards MWC 480

masking.value: Hand-made clean masks; recycled from stronger lines for weaker lines

evidence.quote: We created the `clean`ing masks by hand to cover the emission and little else in each channel.
we subtracted out the continuum using CASA’s `uvcontsub` function

method.value: Self-calibration on continuum, uvcontsub, clean with Briggs weighting

evidence.quote: After self-calibration, we subtracted out the continuum using CASA’s `uvcontsub` function and imaged each targeted line using CASA’s `clean` algorithm.

key_parameters.value: robust 0.5 (2 for weak lines); solint 10-100 s

evidence.quote: Solution intervals were 10-100 seconds.

analysis_steps.goal: Build Keplerian masks and moment-0 maps, spectra and radial profiles

method.value: Keplerian masks from disk geometry with thermal+turbulent broadening; sum within masks; rms maps from 1000 random samples; azimuthal averaging in 0.1" rings

evidence.quote: We created a velocity-integrated emission map (a.k.a. a moment-0 map) for each line and disk pair by summing up the emission within the Keplerian masks across the velocity channels in the data cube.
For all disks, we fixed $r_0$ and $q$ to be 100 AU and -0.3, respectively.

fitting.value: Position and inclination angles from grid search using masks and C18O (12CO or H2CO where necessary)

evidence.quote: we empirically fit for the position and inclination angles using the masks, C$^{18}$O emission towards each disk, and a grid-search algorithm

validation.value: Detection requires peak >=3 sigma and >=3 sigma in at least 4 channels

evidence.quote: Emission within the Keplerian masks is $\geq 3\sigma$ in at least 4 velocity channels of the channel map

method.value: Opacity-corrected rotational diagram linear fit with iterative opacity correction for four disks with >=3 lines

evidence.quote: we initially solve for the opacity-uncorrected $\overline{T_{ex}}$ and $\overline{N_{tot}}$ using a linear fit assuming $C_{\tau_{ul}}=1$, and then we correct the rotational diagram for the opacity using an iterative approach

key_parameters.value: convergence when tau and Tex change at most 0.001% (5000 iterations max for LkCa 15)

evidence.quote: at most 0.001% (or, in the case of the uncertain spike in excitation temperature for LkCa 15, until 5000 iterations have passed)

assumptions.value: LTE, all lines from same environment, emission fills beam; mu=2.37, t0~0.01

evidence.quote: This method assumes that the lines are in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), that all lines originate from the same disk environment, and that the emission fills the beam.

fitting.value: Linear fit of ln(Nu/gu) vs Eu; includes 10% flux uncertainty

evidence.quote: Errors and fits include 10% absolute flux uncertainties, added in quadrature to the velocity-integrated flux uncertainties.

validation.value: Energy ranges similar across disks; critical densities below disk densities supporting LTE

evidence.quote: Notably the energy ranges covered by the H$_2$CO lines for each disk are similar, implying that these results are not due to excitation effects from using different H$_2$CO lines.

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate column density profiles for all disks

method.value: Apply the rotational-diagram equation to single lines with assumed Tex 20-50 K

evidence.quote: we estimate a range of azimuthally-averaged column density profiles using Equation [\[eq_fitline\]](#eq_fitline) for H$_2$CO excitation temperatures between 20-50K.
demonstrating that they are quite insensitive to excitation temperature assumptions in this range

validation.value: Profiles insensitive to Tex in 20-50 K

evidence.quote: demonstrating that they are quite insensitive to excitation temperature assumptions in this range

analysis_steps.goal: Compare H2CO with CO snowline, dust and C18O

method.value: Compare radial profiles with literature/toy-model CO snowline ranges, continuum and C18O profiles

evidence.quote: we compare the observed H$_2$CO emission profiles with estimated locations of CO snowlines at the disk midplane.

assumptions.value: Freeze-out temperature range 17-25 K for model-based snowlines

evidence.quote: we estimate midplane snowlines at locations corresponding to a similar temperature range of 17-25K
we used the COMMON ASTRONOMY SOFTWARE APPLICATIONS package (CASA) version 4.7.2 to self-calibrate and image each targeted line.
The Keplerian mask package is available on GitHub (<https://github.com/jpegues/kepmask>). Version 1.0.0 was used for this paper

results_numeric.quantity: Estimated column density range across sample

evidence.quote: estimated column densities span nearly three orders of magnitude, from $\sim5 - 5000 \times 10^{11}$cm$^{-2}$

results_numeric.value: 13/15 disks with 26 line detections; 11 additional tentative

evidence.quote: We report a total of 26 H$_2$CO detections towards 13/15 disks

findings_qualitative.value: 8/13 detected disks are centrally peaked; about half show outer rings/plateaus

evidence.quote: The majority (8/13) of the disks are centrally peaked in H$_2$CO.

findings_qualitative.value: H2CO emission is present both interior and exterior to the CO snowline in all disks, implying gas-phase and grain-surface formation

evidence.quote: There is significant H$_2$CO emission both interior and exterior to the CO snowline of all disks.

claims.hypothesis: H2CO in disks forms through both gas-phase and CO-ice hydrogenation chemistry
claims.experiment: Compared H2CO radial profiles with estimated CO snowline locations
claims.result: Central emission inside snowline and rings/plateaus at or beyond it in majority of disks
claims.finding: H2CO is commonly produced by both pathways

evidence.quote: The simplest explanation for these H$_2$CO morphologies is that H$_2$CO is produced through both gas-phase and grain-surface chemistry in disks.

claims.hypothesis: H2CO excitation temperatures reflect emission layers
claims.result: Tex 21-37 K for three disks, 11 K for DM Tau
claims.finding: Emission mostly from warm molecular layer, DM Tau from colder midplane

evidence.quote: three are consistent with the warm molecular layer, and one (DM Tau) with the disk midplane

claims.hypothesis: H2CO column density depends on stellar type/age/disk size
claims.experiment: Median column density profiles grouped by age and type
claims.result: Herbig Ae lower than T Tauri; no trend with dust size
claims.finding: Tentative trend with stellar type only (two Herbig Ae disks)

evidence.quote: Note that this trend is tentative, since there are only two Herbig Ae disks in the sample

why_this_method.value: Keplerian masks reduce noise in extracted emission

evidence.quote: ultimately reducing the noise incorporated into the extracted emission

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Dust opacity as cause of central H2CO depressions, rejected for all but IM Lup

evidence.quote: For all disks except IM Lup, optically thick dust is likely not a major cause for the H$_2$CO emission substructure in the sample.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Inheritance of H2CO ice alone cannot explain morphologies

evidence.quote: which suggests that inheritance alone cannot explain the observed H$_2$CO emission morphologies.

limitations_admitted.value: Non-uniform initial calibration across the sample

evidence.quote: we note that this initial calibration was non-uniform across the sample.

limitations_admitted.value: Model-based snowline estimates are very uncertain

evidence.quote: Note that these model-based estimates are very uncertain

referee_caveats_inferred: Only two Herbig Ae disks, so the stellar-type trend is weak
Uniform Tex of 20-50 K assumed for single-line disks
Heterogeneous resolution and missing large-scale flux affect comparisons
Snowline locations from toy models and heterogeneous sources
